query: antitrust lawsuits against Google Amazon Meta Microsoft
normalized: against amazon antitrust google lawsuits meta microsoft

output.content:
**Major U.S. government antitrust actions against the four companies, as of October 17, 2026:** [[1]]

| Company | Principal case(s) | Core allegation / outcome | Current posture |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Google (Alphabet)** | **DOJ and states v. Google—search distribution** (filed 2020) | The D.C. District Court held in August 2024 that Google unlawfully maintained a monopoly in general search and search advertising under Sherman Act §2. [[2]]| In 2026, the court imposed conduct remedies: limits on exclusive distribution contracts involving Search, Chrome, Assistant, and Gemini; specified data-sharing; and search/text-ad syndication obligations. [[2]]|
| **Google (Alphabet)** | **DOJ and states v. Google—ad tech** (filed January 2023) | DOJ and states alleged monopolization of key “ad tech stack” markets used by web publishers to buy and sell digital advertising. [[3]]| The Eastern District of Virginia found Google liable for monopolizing open-web digital-advertising markets, and the 2026 remedy includes interoperability, data-sharing, anti-discrimination, and restrictions on self-preferencing in bidding. [[3]] [[4]]|
| **Amazon** | **FTC, 17 states, and Puerto Rico v. Amazon** (filed September 26, 2023) | The plaintiffs allege Amazon illegally maintained monopoly power in the online-superstore market and in online marketplace services for sellers through interlocking exclusionary and unfair practices. [[5]]| The complaint focuses particularly on alleged anti-discounting tactics and alleged conditioning of Prime eligibility on use of Amazon fulfillment services. [[6]]|
| **Meta** | **FTC v. Meta/Facebook** (filed 2020) | The FTC alleged that Meta maintained a monopoly in personal social networking by acquiring competitive threats Instagram and WhatsApp. [[7]]| Meta won the District Court ruling in November 2025, but the FTC filed an appeal in January 2026 to the D.C. Circuit; thus the government challenge remains unresolved on appeal. [[7]]|
| **Microsoft** | **United States v. Microsoft** (filed May 18, 1998) | The landmark monopolization case challenged Microsoft’s conduct surrounding Windows and browser distribution, with the DOJ complaint filed in the District of Columbia in 1998. [[8]] [[9]]| The case is historical rather than a current operating-business antitrust suit; the DOJ’s final-judgment record identifies it as Civil Action No. 98-1232. [[10]]|
| **Microsoft** | **FTC challenge to Microsoft–Activision Blizzard** | The FTC alleged the acquisition could allow Microsoft to suppress rivals in Xbox consoles, subscriptions, and cloud gaming. [[11]]| Microsoft completed the acquisition of Activision Blizzard on October 13, 2023, for a reported transaction value of $79.6 billion; this was merger enforcement rather than a classic monopolization case. [[12]]|

**Bottom line:** Google faces the most consequential current U.S. antitrust remedies because courts have found liability in both search and open-web ad-tech monopolization matters. [[2]] [[3]] Meta’s central monopolization case is in appellate litigation, Amazon’s marketplace-monopolization case remains the major unresolved federal challenge to its retail platform practices, and Microsoft’s defining monopolization case is historical while its recent major antitrust fight concerned the Activision acquisition. [[7]] [[5]] [[10]] [[11]]
